diagnostics.message:
[merged-gpt-6-luna-atleast2of3]
[final-gpt-6-luna-effort-high-run1]
The HTTP settings deletion can leave its referenced probe in place only after the settings are removed; order the destroy-time operations so HTTP settings are deleted before the probe.

----------------------------------------

[final-gpt-6-luna-effort-high-run2]
`delete_http_settings` removes settings that may reference probes, so its destroy action should run before `delete_probe` removes those probes.

----------------------------------------

[final-gpt-6-luna-effort-high-run3]
The HTTP settings deletion must run before probe deletion because settings can reference a probe; add an explicit ordering dependency from the HTTP-settings deletion resource to the probe deletion resource.

----------------------------------------

[merged-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-atleast2of3]
[final-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-effort-high-run1]
null_resource.delete_http_settings does not depend on null_resource.delete_probe. HTTP settings reference the probe, so on destroy the settings must be removed before the probe. delete_http_settings currently lists null_resource.set_probe instead — a create-only resource with no destroy provisioner — so delete_probe has no incoming ordering and can be destroyed in the first wave, deleting the probe while HTTP settings still reference it (referential-integrity failure). It should depend on null_resource.delete_probe.

----------------------------------------

[final-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-effort-high-run2]
delete_http_settings depends on create-time set_probe, whose destruction is a no-op, so it does not enforce teardown ordering against delete_probe. HTTP settings reference the probe, so delete_http_settings must be destroyed before delete_probe; add delete_probe (or replace set_probe) in depends_on.

----------------------------------------

[final-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-effort-high-run3]
null_resource.delete_http_settings has a destroy-time provisioner that removes an HTTP setting which references a probe on the Application Gateway. The probe must not be removed until after the HTTP setting is gone, so delete_http_settings must be destroyed before delete_probe. It currently depends_on null_resource.set_probe (a create-only resource whose destroy does nothing), which does not order the actual probe deletion. It should depend on null_resource.delete_probe.

----------------------------------------

[merged-glm-5.3-flash-atleast2of3]
[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run1]
delete_http_settings depends on set_probe (a create-time resource) rather than delete_probe. HTTP settings reference probes (PROBE = var.settings.probes[...].name), so on destroy the settings must be removed from the gateway before the probe. Without a dependency on delete_probe, the destroy ordering of delete_http_settings relative to delete_probe is undefined and the settings deletion can run before/while the probe still exists. The existing depends_on entry null_resource.set_probe should be null_resource.delete_probe.

----------------------------------------

[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run2]
resource.null_resource.delete_http_settings has a destroy-time provisioner that deletes HTTP settings which can reference custom probes, but it does not depend on null_resource.delete_probe. Its depends_on list references null_resource.set_probe instead (almost certainly a typo for the delete counterpart), so on destroy the probe can be deleted while HTTP settings referencing it still exist, failing the Application Gateway update (and the provisioner uses on_failure = fail). Adding depends_on on delete_probe ensures HTTP settings are removed before the probe.

----------------------------------------

[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run3]
null_resource.delete_http_settings destroys HTTP settings that reference probes (PROBE = try(each.value.probe, var.settings.probes[each.value.probe_key].name)), but nothing orders null_resource.delete_probe after it on destroy: delete_probe has no depends_on at all, so its destroy-time delete script can run before/out-of-band with the settings deletion, leaving http_settings referencing a deleted probe (and delete_http_settings has on_failure = fail, which can break destroys). delete_http_settings should depend_on null_resource.delete_probe so settings are removed before their probes.

[merged-gpt-6-luna-atleast2of3]
[final-gpt-6-luna-effort-high-run1]
An HTTP listener uses the frontend port, so the listener should be deleted before the frontend port is removed.

----------------------------------------

[final-gpt-6-luna-effort-high-run2]
`delete_http_listener` should be destroyed before `delete_frontend_port`, because listeners reference frontend ports.

----------------------------------------

[final-gpt-6-luna-effort-high-run3]
The HTTP listener must be deleted before its frontend port, but the listener deletion resource is not ordered against the frontend-port deletion resource. Add a dependency so Terraform destroys the listener deletion resource before the frontend-port deletion resource.

----------------------------------------

[merged-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-atleast2of3]
[final-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-effort-high-run1]
null_resource.delete_http_listener does not depend on null_resource.delete_frontend_port. HTTP listeners reference the frontend port, so on destroy the listener must be removed before the frontend port. delete_http_listener currently lists null_resource.set_frontend_port instead — a create-only resource with no destroy provisioner — leaving delete_frontend_port with no incoming ordering, so the port may be deleted while a listener still references it. delete_http_listener should depend on null_resource.delete_frontend_port.

----------------------------------------

[final-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-effort-high-run2]
delete_http_listener depends on create-time set_frontend_port, which has no destroy provisioner, rather than on delete_frontend_port. The listener references the frontend port, so during teardown delete_http_listener must run before delete_frontend_port.

----------------------------------------

[final-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-effort-high-run3]
null_resource.delete_http_listener has a destroy-time provisioner that removes an HTTP listener which references a frontend port. The frontend port cannot be removed until after the listener is gone, so delete_http_listener must be destroyed before delete_frontend_port. It currently depends_on null_resource.set_frontend_port (a create-only resource with no destroy provisioner), which does not order the actual frontend-port deletion. It should depend on null_resource.delete_frontend_port.

----------------------------------------

[merged-glm-5.3-flash-atleast2of3]
[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run1]
delete_http_listener depends on set_frontend_port (create-time) instead of delete_frontend_port. The listener's PORT references var.settings.frontend_ports[...] (or the gateway's frontend port of the same name), so the listener must be deleted from the Application Gateway before the frontend port. delete_frontend_port has no depends_on at all, so its destroy-time provisioner may run in any order relative to the listener deletion; since the listener delete uses on_failure = fail, deleting the port first can fail the destroy. Add depends_on = [null_resource.delete_frontend_port, ...] to delete_http_listener.

----------------------------------------

[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run2]
resource.null_resource.delete_http_listener has a destroy-time provisioner that deletes HTTP listeners which reference frontend ports, but it does not depend on null_resource.delete_frontend_port. Its depends_on list references null_resource.set_frontend_port instead (almost certainly a typo for the delete counterpart), so on destroy the frontend port can be deleted while a listener still references it, failing the Application Gateway update (and the provisioner uses on_failure = fail). Adding depends_on on delete_frontend_port ensures listeners are removed before the frontend port.

----------------------------------------

[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run3]
null_resource.delete_http_listener deletes listeners that reference frontend ports (PORT = try(var.settings.frontend_ports[each.value.front_end_port_key].name, ...)), so the frontend port must be deleted after the listener on destroy. The resource's explicit depends_on includes null_resource.set_frontend_port (keeping the set-resource alive past the listener delete) but not null_resource.delete_frontend_port, the resource that actually performs the deletion; delete_frontend_port has no depends_on and no dependents, so its delete script can race with or precede the listener deletion (delete_http_listener has on_failure = fail). delete_http_listener should also depend_on null_resource.delete_frontend_port.
